sentences.text:
Shri Gaurav Laad,
learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Gaurav Singh Chouhan, learned Government Advocate for the State.
The matter is taken up for hearing, hence I.A.No. 10000/2023, application for urgent hearing stands disposed of.

2. Heard on I.A.No. 6885/2023, which is first application under Section 389 of the Cr.P.C. filed by the appellant-Deepak who stands convicted vide judgment dated 29.06.2022 passed by the Fifth Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act), 2012,
District Indore in Session Trial No. 100/2020 under Section 5(N)(M) read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo 20 years RI with fine of Rs. 500/- and default stipulations.
3.

entities.text:
Fifth Additional Sessions Judge & Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act), 2012,
District Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The prosecution case found to be proved is that the present appellant who is the relative of the prosecutrix, committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon the prosecutrix who was aged about 4 years at the time to incident due to which she sustained injuries, as confirmed by the doctor.
4 . Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the case.

He further submits that there is no allegation of commission of rape against the appellant,
therefore, he has not been convicted under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.
It is only a case that due to some previous enmity, appellant has been implicated.
Appeal is of the year 2023 and its final disposal will take considerable time.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant and release him on bail.

5. Per contra, learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposes the prayer and submits that Dr. Kamini Simlot who medically examined the prosecutrix found that there was a scratch about 2 cm long in the lateral wall of vagina as well as swelling and redness which goes to show that offence has been committed.
The custody period of the appellant is only two years out of the total sentence of 20 years.
Hence, he prays that the application be rejected.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the record.

7. Considering the rival submissions of the counsel for the parties, facts and circumstances of the case, nature & gravity of offence as well as the custody period of the appellant which is less, at this stage we do not find any substantial ground to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant and release Deepak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173790841/
1 him on bail.
8.
